subject.title: Feature request: cron job auto-retry on failure (--retry-count, --retry-delay)

question: Should OpenClaw add per-job cron retry controls on top of shipped global `cron.retry`, and what public CLI/Gateway/storage contract should define count, delay/backoff, defaults, and clear/disable semantics?
rationale: The remaining work changes compatibility-sensitive CLI flags, Gateway schemas, persisted job data, scheduler behavior, and side-effect retry policy, so automation should not choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Approve additive per-job retry policy
options.body: Add job-level retry settings with explicit zero/clear behavior, protocol and docs updates, scheduler tests, and global-default fallback when unset.

options.title: Keep global retry only
options.body: Declare the v2026.6.11 global transient retry behavior sufficient and narrow this request to docs or status visibility if needed.

options.title: Fold into reason-aware guardrails
options.body: Move per-job retry policy into the broader cron guardrail design tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/14376.

recommendation.title: Approve additive per-job retry policy
recommendation.body: Add job-level retry settings with explicit zero/clear behavior, protocol and docs updates, scheduler tests, and global-default fallback when unset.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the merged recurring retry implementation and is closest to the current scheduler/product tradeoff.
